monuments.name: Church of St. Janyl and the Cathedral Hill precinct
monuments.name_ru: Церковь Святой Джаныл и ансамбль Соборного холма
monuments.place: Cathedral Hill, Iyık Janyl
monuments.date: 1727; cloister, seminary, library and archives 18th–20th c.
monuments.wh: World Heritage List, 2004 (Church of St. Janyl and the Ruins of Old Iyık Janyl, one property; United States nomination for the territory)
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl (owner and user)
monuments.zone: Precinct walls; buffer zone to the foot of Cathedral Hill. Works on the fabric only with the Service's written approval.
rules: No photography or filming inside the church during services.
No flash, tripods or lights anywhere inside the church, the library or the archives.
No photography in the seminary library or the cathedral archives at any time.
No drones over Cathedral Hill (the whole buffer zone).
Filming and commercial photography: written consent of the archeparchy and a filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: The precinct is a place of worship. Visitors follow the directions of the sacristans. The 3D virtual tour of the church, made under the World Heritage management plan with the Service as partner, is published by the cathedral.

link.text: Virtual tour on the cathedral's site

monuments.desc: The church built in 1727 by masons who used Islamic building techniques for a Syro-Iradi church, with its Nestorian iconography, the cloister, the seminary, the library and the archives of the archeparchy. Inscribed on the World Heritage List in 2004 together with the ruins of Old Iyık Janyl (97/002). The Old Juniper on the church terrace is a natural monument in its own right (98/014). The archeparchy owns and runs the precinct; the Service is the state body answerable for the listed property, approves works on the fabric and part-funds conservation.

monuments.name: Ruins of Old Iyık Janyl (Shar-i-Kuhna)
monuments.place: West bank river terrace, ~2 km SW of the city centre
monuments.wh: World Heritage List, 2004 (part of the property with 97/001)
monuments.zone: Walled town ~45 ha; no building, digging or grazing inside the walls.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed from the paths.
Metal detectors are prohibited inside the zone and within 500 m of it.
monuments.notice: Keep to the marked paths. Do not climb the walls. Anything found on the ground is state property and is handed to the warden.
monuments.desc: The walled medieval town of the 11th-century Nestorian settlement on the river terrace south-west of the present city, an open archaeological zone surrounded by the southern districts.

monuments.name: Caravanserai of Rabat-i-Safed
monuments.type: Monument of architecture and archaeology; open-air museum
monuments.place: Talas valley, ~25 km E of Talas
monuments.wh: World Heritage List, 2014 (Silk Roads serial property). Listed as a component site by Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan; the Office of the Governor's protest of 2014 stands. The Service manages the site.
monuments.zone: Walls and courtyard; protection zone 300 m from the walls; buffer zone along the old road.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed outside and in the courtyard.
No climbing on the walls, bastions or the portal.
Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: Open-air museum. Open daily 9:00–18:00 (November–March 10:00–16:00). Entrance 20 som, schoolchildren and pensioners free. Guided visits for groups by arrangement with the Service.
monuments.desc: The white limestone caravanserai of the 9th century on the medieval road up the Talas valley, a Sogdian foundation on a square plan about 65 m a side with round corner bastions and one arched portal in the east wall. Conserved by the Service's works of 2010–2014 under Director N. Khudoiberdiev.

monuments.name: Kok-Tash Kariz System
monuments.place: Foothill belt along the Qara-Chik line (sections on the tribal side)
monuments.wh: World Heritage List, 2014 (Silk Roads serial property), with 97/003
monuments.holder: Heritage Protection Service; the galleries still water village fields
monuments.zone: Wells and galleries on the ISEZ side, 50 m either side of the gallery line.
rules: Most of the system lies inside the 12 km restricted zone of the Qara-Chik line. Photography and filming there are prohibited.
Entry into the galleries is prohibited.
Inspections are made only with the Gendarmerie and UNMI.
monuments.notice: The Service does not supervise sections on the tribal side of the line. Visitors may see the restored wells by the road; do not leave it.
monuments.desc: An underground irrigation system of galleries and vertical wells beneath the foothills, part of the 2014 Silk Roads listing. Some galleries still water the fields of the villages above them.

monuments.name: Köhne Diz citadel and the Old City of Talas
monuments.name_ru: Цитадель Кёхне-Диз и Старый город Таласа
monuments.place: Old City, ~1–1.6 km NW–N of Central Square
monuments.date: Medieval citadel; Temir-Kapka and Kalan Darwaza gates
monuments.holder: Mayor's Office of Talas; citadel mound: city museum
monuments.zone: Protected zone ~64 ha. New buildings, extra storeys and changes to street fronts only with the Service's approval.
rules: Photography in the streets is allowed. Ask before photographing courtyards and people.
Digging of any depth in the citadel mound only under an excavation permit.
monuments.notice: Householders in the protected zone apply to the Service before any works on walls, roofs or gates (form HPS-3).
monuments.desc: The citadel mound on the west side of the Old City, the surviving north gate of the outer town wall (Temir-Kapka) and the south gate of the citadel's outer enclosure (Kalan Darwaza), with the lanes and courtyard houses between them. TSU dug the citadel from 1972 to 2005.

monuments.name: Diz-i Safid citadel
monuments.place: Limestone knoll in the middle of the city (park)
monuments.zone: The knoll and its slopes.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed.
monuments.notice: Keep off the walls after rain.
monuments.desc: The Kara-Khanid citadel on its limestone knoll above the Lower Town and the Naryn, kept as a park.

monuments.name: Mausoleum of Kenizek-Khatun (Manas Kümbözü)
monuments.place: Talas valley, ~4 km NE of Rabat-i-Safed
monuments.zone: Mausoleum and the walled garden.
rules: Photography outside is allowed. No photography inside the burial chamber.
No candles, ribbons or offerings on the portal.
monuments.notice: The inscription over the portal names Kenizek-Khatun, daughter of an emir. The Service uses this name. Remove shoes before entering.
monuments.desc: A domed brick mausoleum of the 14th century with a carved terracotta portal. Kyrgyz tradition holds it to be the tomb of Manas; its Arabic inscription names a woman, Kenizek-Khatun.

monuments.name: Juma Mosque of Talas
monuments.place: Old City of Talas, south of the citadel mound
monuments.holder: Spiritual Administration of the Muslims of Irad (user); building state property
monuments.zone: Within the protected zone of the Old City (97/005). The porch and its columns may not be glazed or enclosed.
rules: No photography or filming during prayers.
Remove shoes before entering the prayer hall. Women cover their heads.
Visitors are not admitted at Friday noon prayer.
monuments.notice: A working mosque. Visits outside prayer times by arrangement with the imam-khatib.
monuments.desc: Congregational mosque of the Old City with a columned wooden porch (aivan) of carved poplar columns on stone bases and a brick minaret. Closed in the 1930s and used as a store, reopened for worship in 1992. The top of the minaret fell in the Suusamyr earthquake of August 1992 and was rebuilt in brick from the old photographs.

monuments.name: Church of St. Yuhanna, Talas
monuments.place: Old City of Talas
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl (parish church)
monuments.zone: Within the protected zone of the Old City (97/005); the churchyard and its wall.
rules: No photography or filming during services.
No flash or tripods inside the church.
monuments.notice: A parish church in use. The open-air liturgies of 1990 are marked by a stone in the churchyard.
monuments.desc: The oldest church of the Old City still in use, a brick hall church with a low dome over the sanctuary. Shut from 1937 to 1992. From Easter 1990 priests said open-air liturgies in front of the closed church, the first public services in Talas since the closures; the church was given back to the parish in 1992.

monuments.name: Temir-Kapka gate
monuments.place: North entrance of the Old City of Talas
monuments.zone: The gate, the wall stubs either side and 20 m around. No vehicles over 3.5 t through the gate.
rules: No climbing on the gate or the wall stubs.
Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: Traffic through the gate is one way. Pedestrians use the side passage.
monuments.desc: The only surviving gate of the outer town wall of Kokand Talas, a brick gate tower with a pointed arch and the iron-clad timber leaves that give it its name ("iron gate"). The wall either side was pulled down for streets in the Russian period.

monuments.name: Kara-Khanid minaret site, Talas
monuments.place: Old City of Talas
monuments.zone: The fenced plot and 10 m around it. No digging for services without the Service's supervision.
rules: Do not enter the fenced plot.
Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: The base is shown under a protective roof. Information board in Iradi, Russian and English.
monuments.desc: The octagonal brick base of a Kara-Khanid minaret, with bands of cut-brick ornament, found under a courtyard in the Old City. The oldest standing masonry in Talas and evidence for the medieval town under the Old City.

monuments.name: Mausoleum of Aulie-Ata and the fortress mound
monuments.place: Old core of Aulie-Ata town
monuments.date: Mausoleum 11th–12th c., rebuilt; fortress 1850s on an older mound
monuments.holder: Heritage Protection Service; the mausoleum is a place of pilgrimage for local Muslims
monuments.zone: The mausoleum, the mound and the Russian-period streets round the bazaar (protected zone ~18 ha).
rules: Remove shoes inside the mausoleum.
No photography of pilgrims at prayer without their consent.
monuments.notice: The mausoleum is a place of prayer. The mound is unstable on its north side; keep to the paths.
monuments.desc: The domed mausoleum of a Kara-Khanid ruler venerated as Aulie-Ata ("holy father"), round which the town grew, and the mound of the Kokand fortress of the 1850s, taken by the Russians in 1864. Some Russian and Soviet scholars placed medieval Taraz under the mound; Iradi historiography places Taraz at Talas. The Register records the site without taking a side.

monuments.name: Old City bathhouse (moncho) and the Sarchashma Springs
monuments.place: Old City of Talas, below the citadel mound
monuments.holder: Mayor's Office of Talas (owner); bathhouse let to an operator
monuments.zone: The bathhouse, the springs and the brick channels between them.
rules: No photography inside the bathhouse.
Do not wash, water animals or throw coins in the springs.
monuments.notice: The bathhouse is open to the public: men's and women's days alternate.
monuments.desc: A domed brick bathhouse fed by the citadel springs through brick channels, restored and reopened in 2014 with the spring water piped again. Old Talas families still take a bride there before the wedding.

monuments.name: The Old Juniper (Kart Archa)
monuments.place: Church terrace, north of the west steps, Cathedral Hill
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl
monuments.zone: The tree and the ground under its crown.
rules: Do not cut, break or take branches. Only the sacristan gathers fallen twigs.
Do not lean on the iron crutch (1911).
monuments.notice: Inside the World Heritage precinct (97/001); the precinct rules apply.
monuments.desc: A Zeravshan juniper about 14 m high, the oldest living thing in the precinct; its north limb has rested on an iron crutch since 1911.

monuments.name: Ravine cells of the Talas Alatau and the Chatkal (group, 12 sites)
monuments.name_ru: Пещерные кельи Таласского Алатау и Чаткала (группа, 12 объектов)
monuments.district: Talas and Sary-Bulak Districts; the Chatkal
monuments.place: Limestone gorges (locations not published)
monuments.holder: Heritage Protection Service; several are pilgrimage stops
monuments.zone: Each cell and 50 m around it.
rules: Locations are not published to protect the sites.
Cells in use by monks of the Order are not open to visitors.
No photography or filming of occupied cells.
monuments.notice: Pilgrims follow the Order's routes. Do not remove stones, crosses or votive objects.
monuments.desc: Twelve of the hermitages in the limestone gorges used by Christians who worshipped in secret after Timur and by monks and priests hiding in the 1930s. About forty are known; the twelve entered here are those the Service has surveyed.

monuments.name: Korgon of the Abdrai captains
monuments.place: Below the old Talas forts, west of the city
monuments.holder: Abdrai Heritage Foundation (user, under agreement with the Service)
monuments.zone: The walls of the korgon and 50 m around them.
rules: The gate tower is open on Saturdays 10:00-15:00 and by arrangement.
Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: Restoration of the gate tower by the Abdrai Heritage Foundation was approved by the Service (form HPS-3).
monuments.desc: The walled farmstead (korgon) that was the seat of the Abdrai line of mingbashy, captains of the Christian Iradi horse of the Khanate of Kokand from the firman of 1730 until Chernyayev took the Talas forts in 1864. Rammed-earth walls with corner towers and a brick gate tower. The only building of the Kokand period in Irad tied to a Christian office.

monuments.name: Old cemetery of Cathedral Hill
monuments.place: North slope of Cathedral Hill, Iyık Janyl
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl
monuments.zone: Within the buffer zone of the World Heritage property (97/001).
rules: No photography of funerals or memorial services.
Do not touch or rub the gravestones.
monuments.notice: A consecrated burial ground. Visitors keep to the paths.
monuments.desc: Burial ground of the bishops and clergy of Iyık Janyl before the closures of 1937, with carved stones in Syriac and Iradi. Mar Gewargis and three of his successors lie in the church crypt; most of the other bishops and clergy before 1937 lie here.

monuments.name: Motherhouse of the Order of St. Janyl
monuments.place: Edge of the Naryn gorge below Cathedral Hill, Iyık Janyl
monuments.zone: The enclosure wall and the buildings inside it.
rules: The enclosure is closed to visitors except the chapel.
No photography of the sisters or brothers without consent.
monuments.notice: A religious house. The chapel is open for services.
monuments.desc: Motherhouse of the Order of St. Janyl. Its women's branch opened a school for deaf girls here in 1926, where the sisters made the sign vocabulary from which Iradi Sign Language grew; the school was closed in 1937.

monuments.name: Chapel of St. Gewargis, Bazar-Korgon
monuments.place: Outside Bazar-Korgon
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl
monuments.zone: The chapel and its yard.
rules: No photography during services.
monuments.notice: The key is kept in the parish. Damage to the chapel should be reported to the Service and the police.
monuments.desc: Small domed brick chapel on the edge of Bazar-Korgon, one of the few Christian buildings of the Fergana rim farm belt. When a horse skull was nailed over its door in March 2016, men from the town mosque helped take it down.

monuments.name: Chapel at Kochkor-Ata
monuments.place: Kochkor-Ata
monuments.holder: Syro-Iradi Catholic Archeparchy of Iyık Janyl
monuments.zone: The chapel and its yard.
rules: No photography during services.
monuments.notice: The key is kept in the parish.
monuments.desc: Village chapel of the Christian minority of Kochkor-Ata, a mainly Muslim town of the Lower Naryn.

monuments.name: Kand-i Kohna town mound
monuments.place: Talas River terrace, ~6 km W of central Talas
monuments.zone: The mound and 100 m around it.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed.
Metal detectors prohibited.
monuments.notice: No vehicles on the mound.
monuments.desc: A town mound with layers from the Saka period through the Sogdian and early Islamic periods.

monuments.name: Shahr-i Buzurg town site
monuments.place: Beside Shaar-Döbö, ~15 km WNW of Nurzhan
monuments.zone: Citadel, shahristan and suburb, 100 m around the ramparts.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed.
Metal detectors prohibited.
monuments.notice: Grazing on the ramparts is prohibited. Herders are asked to keep stock off the citadel.
monuments.desc: A walled Sogdian and Kara-Khanid town with a citadel mound, a mudbrick shahristan and an outer suburb.

monuments.name: Coppersmiths' Row
monuments.place: Old City of Talas, towards Bazar-i Kalan
monuments.holder: Mayor's Office of Talas; shops privately held
monuments.zone: Within the protected zone of the Old City (97/005). Shopfronts follow the Service's rules for the row.
rules: Ask before photographing craftsmen at work.
monuments.notice: A working street. Signs and awnings need the Service's approval.
monuments.desc: Street of coppersmiths' and tinsmiths' workshops with timber shopfronts and shutters, still worked by a few families.

monuments.name: Iradi Telegraph Office
monuments.place: Old City of Talas
monuments.zone: Within the protected zone of the Old City (97/005).
rules: Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: The building is not open to visitors.
monuments.desc: Brick telegraph office of the Russian period in the Old City, one of the first public buildings of the town to carry an Iradi name.

monuments.name: Houses of the 1860s Russian town, Talas (group)
monuments.name_ru: Жилые дома русского города 1860-х гг., Талас (группа)
monuments.place: Soviet Centre, east of Central Square
monuments.holder: Private owners and the Mayor's Office of Talas
monuments.zone: Each listed house and its street front. Porches, window frames and roofs keep their form and material.
rules: The houses are private. Photograph from the street only.
monuments.notice: Owners may apply to the Service for help with repairs to carved window frames and porches.
monuments.desc: Single-storey brick houses of the colonial grid town laid out east of the Kokand fort after 1864, with iron-roofed porches and carved window frames. The listed group covers the best-kept houses.

monuments.name: Walled farmsteads of Korgoncho (group)
monuments.place: Korgoncho village
monuments.zone: Walls and gateways of each listed farmstead.
rules: The farmsteads are lived in. Photograph from the street unless invited.
monuments.notice: Repairs with cement render are not permitted on the listed walls.
monuments.desc: Rammed-earth walled farmsteads of the Uzbek-speaking village of Korgoncho, which takes its name from them; the best surviving group of Kokand-era rural houses in Irad.

monuments.name: Potters' kilns of Sopol-Tepa (group)
monuments.place: Sopol-Tepa village; clay pits at the Chopo-Jar bluffs
monuments.zone: Each listed kiln and its yard.
rules: Ask before photographing in the potters' yards.
monuments.notice: Working kilns. Keep clear when a kiln is being fired.
monuments.desc: Domed wood-fired kilns of the Uzbek-speaking potters of Sopol-Tepa, who dig their clay at the Chopo-Jar bluffs.

monuments.name: Shelji silver-mining town
monuments.place: Upper Talas valley, ~8 km E of Kümüshtü
monuments.holder: Heritage Protection Service; TSU excavation since 2005
monuments.zone: Town ~20 ha, the slag heaps and the galleries in the hills.
rules: Entry into the old mine galleries is prohibited (collapse).
Photography for private use is allowed on the town site.
monuments.notice: The TSU dig is open to visitors on Saturdays in July and August.
monuments.desc: The citadel mound, walled town and workshop quarters of a medieval silver-mining town named by the Arab geographers.

monuments.name: Kara-Bulak kurgans
monuments.place: Near Kara-Bulak, beside the Trans-Talas Highway
monuments.zone: Burial ground and 50 m around it.
rules: Photography for private use is allowed.
Ploughing and digging prohibited.
monuments.notice: Do not drive over the mounds.
monuments.desc: A burial ground of earth mounds of the Saka period.

monuments.name: Central Square of Talas (place of the events of 1956, 1989 and 1992)
monuments.name_ru: Центральная площадь Таласа (место событий 1956, 1989 и 1992 гг.)
monuments.place: Central Square, Talas
monuments.zone: The square and the façades round it. Changes to the paving, monuments and façades need the Service's approval.
rules: Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: Memorial plaques on the square list the dates. Public events need the Mayor's Office's permission.
monuments.desc: The square of the 1956 Talas riots, of the first open commemoration of them on 14 June 1989 (about 20,000 people), and of the December 1991 protests that began the Winter Uprising of 1992.

monuments.name: Kobozev railhead battlefield and the cairn of Kudaibergen Baatyr
monuments.name_ru: Место боя у Кобозевского железнодорожного узла и курган-памятник Кудайбергена-батыра
monuments.place: Railway approaches to Nurzhan
monuments.zone: The cairn and 50 m around it. The railway right of way is not open to visitors.
rules: Do not cross the railway tracks.
No photography of railway installations.
monuments.notice: A memorial gathering is held at the cairn each 28 July.
monuments.desc: Ground of the fighting for the Kobozev railhead at the end of July 1992, the deadliest action of Operation Starlight, where the Boztorgoy war leader Kudaibergen Duishön uulu (1961–1992) was killed on 28 July. The stone cairn raised in his memory is honoured on both sides of the line.

monuments.name: Kobozev radio mast
monuments.place: Nurzhan
monuments.zone: The mast, its anchor blocks and the guy-wire field.
rules: No climbing. No entry inside the guy-wire field.
Filming and commercial photography: filming permit from the Service.
monuments.notice: The mast is no longer used for broadcasting.
monuments.desc: Steel lattice radio mast of 1934, among the first works of the planned city of Kobozev and for decades its tallest structure. Carried the republic's first radio broadcasts.

monuments.name: Building of the Talas Opera and Ballet Theater
monuments.name_ru: Здание Таласского театра оперы и балета
monuments.place: Central avenue, Talas
monuments.zone: The building and the forecourt.
rules: No photography during performances.
monuments.notice: A working theatre.
monuments.desc: Stalinist-classical theatre building with a columned portico, opened in 1959; the ballet school followed in 1962.

monuments.name: Oktyabr cinema
monuments.place: Cinema Boulevard, Talas
monuments.zone: The building and its street front.
rules: No photography or filming during screenings.
monuments.notice: A working cinematheque.
monuments.desc: Talasfilm's premiere house, where the studio's films opened (among them the films of 1979), since 1996 the cinematheque of the Talasfilm Archives.

monuments.name: Building of the Pushkin Library, Nurzhan
monuments.place: 9 Azatlık Prospect, Nurzhan
monuments.date: Soviet period (State Republican Library of the Iradi SSR, founded 1934)
monuments.zone: The building and its street front.
rules: No photography in the reading rooms.
monuments.notice: Open in library hours.
monuments.desc: Home of the State Republican Library of the Iradi SSR named after A. S. Pushkin, now the Nurzhan branch of the National Library (Russian and technical collections).

monuments.name: Bath No. 3, Vokzal Square
monuments.place: Vokzal Square, Nurzhan
monuments.holder: Nurzhan City Hall (owner); let to an operator
monuments.zone: The building and its façade on Vokzal Square.
rules: No photography inside the baths.
monuments.notice: Open to the public.
monuments.desc: Soviet public baths of 1958 on the station square, with their original façade and lettering.

monuments.name: Headframe of Shaft No. 1 "Pioneer" and the miners' memorial, Rudnik
monuments.name_ru: Копёр шахты № 1 «Пионер» и памятник горнякам, Рудник
monuments.type: Monument of science and technology; monument of history
monuments.place: Rudnik, Sary-Bulak works settlement
monuments.zone: The headframe and the memorial. The works area beyond is not open to visitors.
rules: Do not enter the works area.
No photography of the works beyond the memorial.
monuments.notice: The memorial lists the miners killed at the Combine, including the four of February 2012.
monuments.desc: Steel headframe of the first shaft of the Sary-Bulak antimony works (1961), kept when the shaft closed, and the miners' memorial unveiled beside it in 2013. The museum of the labour collective in the Rudnik house of culture keeps the first ingot of 1964.

monuments.name: Memorial to the Defenders of Talas
monuments.place: East end of Liberty Boulevard, Talas
monuments.zone: The memorial and its paved square.
rules: No climbing on the memorial.
monuments.notice: Wreaths are laid on 18 June, the day the siege of 1992 was broken.
monuments.desc: Bronze memorial to the defenders of Talas in the siege of 10 April – 18 June 1992, cast by Arman Kadir.

monuments.name: "Kara Kyzgaldak" (Black Tulip) memorial, Nurzhan
monuments.place: Nurzhan
monuments.holder: Union of Afghan War Veterans of Irad (user); Nurzhan City Hall
monuments.zone: The memorial and its square.
monuments.notice: The veterans' union meets at the memorial each 15 February.
monuments.desc: Memorial to the soldiers from the Iradi SSR killed in Afghanistan in 1979–89 (about 210 by the veterans' count), named after the aircraft that carried the coffins home.

monuments.name: Building of the Irad Palace of Art
monuments.place: Cathedral Street 4, Iyık Janyl
monuments.date: Soviet period (former district House of Culture)
monuments.zone: The building and its street front, within the buffer zone of the World Heritage property (97/001).
rules: Photography in the galleries follows the museum's rules.
monuments.notice: Open in museum hours.
monuments.desc: The former district House of Culture opposite the cathedral park, home of the Irad Palace of Art.

monuments.name: House of Kemel Ishakov and his grave, Arsha-Say
monuments.name_ru: Дом-музей Кемела Исхакова и его могила, Арша-Сай
monuments.place: Arsha-Say village, on State Route 1
monuments.zone: The house, the yard and the grave.
rules: No flash inside the house.
monuments.notice: Open Wednesday to Sunday. Ask at the village council if the house is shut.
monuments.desc: Birthplace and family house of the national novelist Kemel Ishakov (1930–2009), opened as a house-museum in 2012, and his grave in the village.

monuments.name: Rock-art shelters of the Talas Alatau (group)
monuments.place: Taldy-Bulak valley (lower part); the Kyzyl-Üngkür shelter; the Kara-Suu Canyon entrance (from 2026)
monuments.date: Bronze Age, Saka and Turkic periods
monuments.zone: Each panel or boulder and 30 m around it; the painted shelter behind a fence.
rules: Painted shelter (Kyzyl-Üngkür): no photography. Light damages the ochre. Visits only with a warden.
Pecked boulders: photography for private use is allowed without flash. Do not wet, chalk, rub or trace the images.
Rock art on the tribal side of the line is not supervised by the Service.
monuments.notice: Damage to rock art is an offence under the 1997 heritage ordinance. The Kara-Suu Canyon panels, damaged in places by graffiti and road works, are under provisional protection while the Service surveys them.
monuments.desc: Several hundred pecked images of ibex, deer, horses, archers, solar signs and two-wheeled chariots on dark-varnished boulders, and one shelter with paintings in red ochre. The Kara-Suu Canyon entrance panels were added to the group in 2026.

monuments.name: Terminal of Kobozev Airport
monuments.place: Aeroport, north-west of Nurzhan
monuments.zone: The terminal and its forecourt.
rules: No admission: the building is unsafe.
No photography of the NurGaz heliport.
monuments.notice: The building is fenced. The Service has asked for the roof to be made weathertight.
monuments.desc: Modernist terminal of the old Kobozev Airport (1968), closed in 1992. The apron is now the Aeroport car market.

monuments.name: Ruined chapel at Tegirmen
monuments.place: Hillside above Tegirmen, Talas valley
monuments.zone: The ruin and 100 m around it.
rules: No digging and no metal detectors. Offenders will be reported to the police.
monuments.notice: Finds made here are to be declared to the Service within ten days (2010 amendment).
monuments.desc: Ruins of a stone chapel in the Talas valley, below which a herder found a 17th-c. silver chalice and paten in 2025. Entered provisionally while the site is surveyed.

monuments.name: Kara-Suu I cave shelter (excavation)
monuments.place: Kara-Suu Canyon mouth, above the Sary-Bulak road
monuments.holder: Heritage Protection Service; excavation by TSU, Department of Archaeology
monuments.zone: Fenced excavation and 100 m around it. Road works within the zone are coordinated with the Service.
rules: Closed site. No admission beyond the fence.
No photography or filming of the excavation, the trenches or the finds.
Press visits only through the Service.
monuments.notice: Excavation permit No. 07/2026 (rescue excavation). Finds are recorded and go to the Service's store; results will be published by TSU. The site is next to the Gendarmerie control post; follow the post's instructions.
monuments.noimg: Photography of the excavation is not permitted.
monuments.desc: A limestone cave shelter at the canyon mouth found during rockfall clearing on the Sary-Bulak road. Trial trenches in September 2026 found hearths and pottery. Entered provisionally while the excavation lasts.

unlisted: Sites on the tribal side of the Qara-Chik line (Bitik-Tash, Kara-Unkur Cave and others) are recorded in the Archaeological Map of the Karatau and the Kyzylkum Fringe (TSU, 2009) but are not entered in the Register: the Service does not work beyond the line.
